events.title: The earliest recorded Christmas on 25 December
events.description: A Roman calendar compiled in 354 records the birth of Christ celebrated in Rome on 25 December 336, the earliest evidence for the date. Why it was chosen remains debated.
events.html: A Roman calendar compiled in 354 records the birth of Christ celebrated in Rome on 25 December 336, the earliest evidence for the date. Why it was chosen remains debated.

events.title: Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne emperor
events.description: During Christmas Mass in St Peter's, Leo III crowned the Frankish king Charlemagne Emperor of the Romans. It revived a western imperial title unused since 476.
events.html: During Christmas Mass in St Peter's, Leo III crowned the Frankish king Charlemagne Emperor of the Romans. It revived a western imperial title unused since 476.

events.title: Emperor Leo V is murdered in the Great Palace of Constantinople
events.description: Followers of Michael II murdered the Byzantine emperor Leo V the Armenian in a church of the Great Palace of Constantinople. Michael took the throne as the first ruler of the Amorian dynasty.
events.html: Followers of Michael II murdered the Byzantine emperor Leo V the Armenian in a church of the Great Palace of Constantinople. Michael took the throne as the first ruler of the Amorian dynasty.

events.title: Stephen I is crowned the first king of Hungary
events.description: Stephen I, son of Grand Prince Géza, was crowned at Esztergom as the first king of Hungary, which became a Christian kingdom. The coronation is dated either 25 December 1000 or 1 January 1001.
events.html: Stephen I, son of Grand Prince Géza, was crowned at Esztergom as the first king of Hungary, which became a Christian kingdom. The coronation is dated either 25 December 1000 or 1 January 1001.

events.title: Mieszko II Lambert is crowned king of Poland at Gniezno
events.description: Mieszko II Lambert, son of Bolesław I the Brave, was crowned King of Poland in Gniezno Cathedral. His reign saw attacks by the Holy Roman Empire and Kievan Rus, revolts by his brothers and the loss of the royal crown.
events.html: Mieszko II Lambert, son of Bolesław I the Brave, was crowned King of Poland in Gniezno Cathedral. His reign saw attacks by the Holy Roman Empire and Kievan Rus, revolts by his brothers and the loss of the royal crown.

events.title: Pope Clement II crowns Henry III emperor
events.description: Henry III, king of Germany since 1039, was crowned Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Clement II, the former bishop of Bamberg, whom Henry had made pope after the Synod of Sutri removed three rival claimants.
events.html: Henry III, king of Germany since 1039, was crowned Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Clement II, the former bishop of Bamberg, whom Henry had made pope after the Synod of Sutri removed three rival claimants.

events.title: William the Conqueror is crowned at Westminster
events.description: William of Normandy was crowned king of England in Westminster Abbey. Norman soldiers, mistaking the congregation's acclamation for a riot, set fire to nearby houses.
events.html: William of Normandy was crowned king of England in Westminster Abbey. Norman soldiers, mistaking the congregation's acclamation for a riot, set fire to nearby houses.

events.title: Washington crosses the Delaware
events.description: On Christmas night, George Washington led about 2,400 soldiers across the ice-choked Delaware River. At dawn they surprised the Hessian garrison at Trenton.
events.html: On Christmas night, George Washington led about 2,400 soldiers across the ice-choked Delaware River. At dawn they surprised the Hessian garrison at Trenton.

events.title: Mikhail Gorbachev resigns as Soviet president
events.description: In a televised address, Mikhail Gorbachev resigned. That evening the Soviet flag was lowered from the Kremlin and replaced by the Russian tricolour.
